subject: Runtime degradation impacting BlueLoom inference requests - customer brief & follow-up

From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>

Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-07-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: [URGENT] Runtime degradation observed for BlueLoom - starting bridge

Irene / Marissa —

We observed a widespread increase in 95th/99th percentile latencies for the BlueLoom account starting ~08:56 PT. Error rates are low (~0.4%) but the latency spike has caused timeouts within their product gateway; they’ve reported degraded user experience.

What we’ve done so far:
- Identified a change in batch sizing behavior for a subset of inference workers after a memory reclaim at 08:51 PT.
- Temporarily disabled the aggressive batching heuristic on the affected pool (08:59 PT) — this reduced latency for a small set of traffic but the broader roll is still showing pressure.
- Opened bridge (phone + Zoom) and running continuous sampling of slow traces.

Immediate asks:
- Can you join the bridge for a 9:20 sync? Need decisions on whether to failover BlueLoom to a different pool and whether to enable a temporary routing rule to reduce max sequences per batch.
- Please review the attached bridge_log.txt and mitigation_patch.diff (small runtime tweak we can push as a hotfix).

Impact: customer session timeouts and higher end-user latency reported. Estimated affected requests: ~2.5% of BlueLoom traffic (skewed to longer sequences).

Diego
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: bridge_log.txt (6KB), mitigation_patch.diff (3KB)

Date: 2025-07-19T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Runtime degradation impacting BlueLoom inference requests - customer brief & follow-up

Hi Emily / BlueLoom ops team —

First, I want to apologize for the disruption this morning. We understand this impacted your end users and are treating this with highest priority. Brief summary for your team:

- What happened: a subset of our inference workers entered an aggressive-batching state after a memory reclaim which increased queueing latency for longer sequences.
- Customer impact: intermittent timeouts and elevated response latency for longer requests beginning ~08:56 PT.
- Current status: mitigation in progress (we’ve disabled the heuristic on the affected pool and are testing a hotfix). We’ve also started a controlled failover to a secondary GPU pool to restore normal latency for the majority of your traffic.
- ETA for stable recovery: we expect the targeted failover and hotfix rollout to finish within 2 hours; I will update you by 11:45 PT or sooner if we have earlier confirmation.

Next steps / how we’ll keep you informed:
- Live bridge (zoom + dial-in) is open — join link: https://zoom.redwood.example.com/bridges/BL-7083
- I’ll send a post-incident summary and proposed remediation plan once we close the bridge.
- If you prefer, we can schedule an executive review call later today to discuss impacts and remediation timelines.

As an immediate goodwill gesture we will apply a one-time service credit to offset the visible user impact; I’ll confirm the amount in the follow-up.

Thank you for your patience.

—
Irene Choi
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Subject: Post-incident update: timeline, root cause hypothesis, and next steps (BlueLoom)

Hi Emily / BlueLoom ops —

Thank you again for the time on Monday’s post-incident review. This is the follow-up with our confirmed timeline, root cause analysis, and remediation plan.

Summary (short):
- Incident window: 2025-07-19 08:56 PT — 2025-07-19 11:10 PT (service impact cleared after full failover and rollout of the mitigation).
- Root cause: a race between memory reclaim and our dynamic batching heuristic that left a subset of workers with unusually large batch sizes; this amplified queueing for long-sequence requests.
- Corrective actions (already completed):
  * Disabled aggressive-batching heuristic as default for affected pools.
  * Full failover to pool-eu-standby completed at 10:58 PT.
  * Hotfix rollout to runtime fleet completed at 11:06 PT.
- Follow-on work (RCA owners assigned):
  1) Add a safety check into the batching heuristic to prevent growth post-reclaim (Owner: Diego).
  2) Add additional telemetry for sequence-length distribution in routing layer (Owner: Marissa).
  3) Update our incident runbook to include an explicit failover decision checklist (Owner: Monica).

We’ve uploaded the full draft postmortem and a CSV timeline to the shared folder: https://drive.redwood.example.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-blueloom-postmortem

Per our commitment, we will apply a one-time service credit equal to 25% of BlueLoom’s July usage for the impacted SLA window. Finance will follow up to confirm the credit posting timeframe.

If you’d like a deeper technical walkthrough with the runtime team we can schedule that for later this week.

Thanks again for your partnership — we own this and will publish the final postmortem once RCA work is complete.

Best,

Irene Choi
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: postmortem-draft.pdf, incident_timeline.csv
